newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW reach tentative deal at Indiana plant.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW reach tentative deal at Indiana plant.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Thursday it reached a tentative agreement with the United Auto Workers union to end a strike at the automaker's Fort Wayne, Ind., pickup truck plant.
The deal was expected to be put up for a ratification vote by union members later Thursday, said Tom Beaman, communications manager at the GM Truck Group in Pontiac, Mich.
"If the agreement is ratified by the work force, employees will return to work at their regular shift starting times on Tuesday, April 1," Beaman said.
He declined to comment on the content of the agreement.
The strike started Friday, March 14, when 2,700 GM employees walked off the job, marking the first local contract dispute since GM reached a new three-year, national labour pact last November.
Workers at the plant make Chevrolet C/K and GMC Sierra regular-cab, full-size pickup trucks. About 1,000 units per day are produced.
